LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.symbolCount: The count of a letter a in a length-n word x is the number of positions i at which x(i) = a.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.symbolCount_zero: Every letter occurs zero times in the empty word.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.sum_symbolCount: For a word of length n on a finite alphabet, the sum of all its letter counts is n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.wordTypes: The length-n types on a finite alphabet A are all functions that assign a nonnegative integer count to each letter, with counts summing to n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mem_wordTypes: A function from the finite alphabet A to the nonnegative integers belongs to the set of length-n types exactly when its counts sum to n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.wordTypes_zero: At length zero the only type on a finite alphabet is the function assigning zero to every letter.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.wordType: The type of a word on a finite alphabet is its vector of letter counts. These counts sum to the word length n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.wordType_surjecti: Every length-n type on a finite alphabet is the type of at least one word of length n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.typeClass: The type class of t is the set of all length-n words on the alphabet whose vector of letter counts is t.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mem_typeClass: A word belongs to the type class of t if and only if its vector of letter counts equals t.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.existsUnique_mem_: Each length-n word on a finite alphabet belongs to exactly one of its length-n type classes.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.symbolCount_comp_: Permuting a word’s positions leaves the number of occurrences of every letter unchanged.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.wordType_comp_per: Permuting the positions of a word on a finite alphabet preserves its type.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.card_wordTypes_le: The number of types at length n on a finite alphabet A is at most (n + 1)^|A|.
